cse-2011-cs-3.approach: Use conditional probability on the reduced sample space: conditioning on "at least one head" removes TT and leaves three equally likely outcomes.

steps.title: Sample space
steps.body: Two fair coins: $\{HH, HT, TH, TT\}$, each with probability $\tfrac14$.

steps.title: Condition
steps.body: "At least one head" $=\{HH, HT, TH\}$, so $P(\text{cond}) = \tfrac34$.

steps.title: Compute
steps.body: $$P(HH \mid \ge 1\,H) = \frac{P(HH)}{P(\ge 1\,H)} = \frac{1/4}{3/4} = \frac13$$

optionAnalysis.reason: Correct: one favourable outcome (HH) out of three equally likely outcomes.
$1/4$ is the unconditional probability of HH; it ignores the given information.
$1/2$ comes from wrongly treating "the other coin" as independent of the condition (that would be the answer if a *specific* coin were known to be a head).
$2/3$ is the probability of exactly one head given at least one head.

pitfalls: Confusing "at least one is a head" with "the first coin is a head" (which gives 1/2).
